verdict: Starbucks grew revenue 8% to a record $9.4B as global comparable sales rose 5%, and wider margins lifted net earnings 20% to $1.0B.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: vs a year ago — a quarterly record

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Coffeehouses in the U.S. and Canada — comparable store sales rose 5% on a 4% higher average ticket and 1% more transactions, plus new stores.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Coffeehouses outside North America — comparable sales rose 7%, with China up 10% on 21% more transactions partly offset by a 9% lower ticket.

segments.name: Channel Development
segments.note: Packaged coffee and ready-to-drink drinks sold in grocery and convenience stores — down after the sale of the Seattle's Best Coffee brand and softer ready-to-drink sales.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: Small leftover businesses and unallocated items.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — support centers and head office, including higher spending behind the Reinvention plan.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on coffeehouses, roasteries and equipment.

otherDetail: Income from equity investees of $56M and $34M of interest and other income, less $140M of interest expense.
follow100Note: Net earnings of $1,024M are essentially all attributable to Starbucks. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Reported operating income of $1,485M includes $56M of income from equity investees, shown here in Other income. Starbucks reports in tenths of a million; this page rounds to whole millions (reported net earnings were $1,024.4M, all attributable to Starbucks).

takeaways.title: Customers came more often and spent more
takeaways.text: Global comparable store sales rose 5% — transactions up 3% and average ticket up 2%. North America rose 5%, International 7%, and China 10% as transactions there jumped 21%.

takeaways.title: Margins widened
takeaways.text: GAAP operating margin expanded 140 basis points to 15.8% on sales leverage and in-store efficiency work under the Reinvention plan, partly offset by higher store wages and benefits. North America's margin reached 21.4%.

takeaways.title: Loyalty kept growing, stores kept opening
takeaways.text: U.S. Starbucks Rewards 90-day active members rose 13% to 34.3 million, and Starbucks opened 549 net new stores to end the quarter with 38,587 — 51% company-operated and 49% licensed.
